title: Longest Increasing Subsequence II
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the length of the longest subsequence that is strictly increasing and where the difference between consecutive elements is at most k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the length of the longest subsequence that is strictly increasing and where the difference between consecutive elements is at most k. A subsequence is formed by removing some or no elements from the original array while preserving the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: nums is nonempty and contains positive integers; k is positive.
The subsequence preserves input order, increases strictly, and each adjacent difference is at most k.
hints: For a new value v, only earlier sequence endings in [v-k,v-1] may precede it.
Store the best length by ending value in a range-maximum segment tree over compressed values.
Query the valid predecessor interval, add one, and point-update v without lowering an existing best.
The DP recurrence is exact, and the segment tree replaces its linear predecessor scan with logarithmic range queries while input-order processing preserves subsequence order.
editorial: The DP recurrence is exact, and the segment tree replaces its linear predecessor scan with logarithmic range queries while input-order processing preserves subsequence order.

tests.explanation: One longest valid subsequence is [1,3,4,5,8], whose length is five.
The jump from one to five exceeds k, so either single element is optimal.
